absent: Full VNCR translation walk combining guest stage-1 and stage-2, fault status encoding, and write descriptor layout.
Exact nested permission fault synthesis and ESR fault code selection for read versus write violations.
Complete pkvm mapping object layout beyond frame, count, physical frame and coherency attributes, and the unshare path.
PMU backing perf event creation, release and period computation lifecycle.
Hypercall ABIs for protection finalize, teardown, reclaim, write-protect, young tracking and permission relaxation.
ID register field positions, mask constant values and CPU capability detection details.

findings.text: Nested VNCR abort entry first confirms the fault reports VNCR state and offloads external aborts on the data path. It only accepts translation and permission fault classes and otherwise reports an internal error. It speculatively pins the per-VM TLB epoch across translation so concurrent invalidations take a slow path, releases the pin on translation failure, retries on transient contention or host allocation shortage, asks userspace to resolve guest-memfd backing failures, reinjects decoded fault status toward nested EL2 when translation is impossible, and otherwise validates read or write permission before raising a nested permission fault.

Nested ID register sanitizer takes a raw feature register value and returns a constrained value for exposure to a nested hypervisor. It clears unsupported instruction, memory, debug and trace extensions, forces all exception levels to 64-bit only, hides selected granule and security extensions, clamps enumerated fields such as counter offset, address range, hardware update, translation lifetime, nested virtualization fractional version and debug version to supported ceilings, derives granule availability from host page size and original value, and selects either a VHE with limited nested virtualization personality or an E2H0-only personality based on vCPU feature state and final CPU capabilities.

Field limiter reads the current enumerated value of a named ID field, clears that field in the accumulator, then writes back the smaller of the observed value and a supplied architectural ceiling. It preserves all other bits and returns the updated register word for further sanitization.

Named trap mask constant selects the set of monitor debug controls that a nested guest is allowed to influence. It covers debug, trace and performance monitoring trap controls plus debug communications and OS lock related traps, combined as a single bitmask for use when virtualizing nested debug state.

Protected-mode indicator is a global static branch initially false, with a shared pointer to the hypervisor-visible memblock array. The base address and size of the reserved hypervisor region are global physical quantities set during early reservation and later excluded from introspection.

Early reservation runs only when hypervisor mode is available, the kernel is not already in hypervisor mode, and protected mode is selected. It copies host memory regions into the hypervisor-visible array with a fixed capacity, sums page needs for hypervisor and host stage-two tables plus VM metadata, vmemmap, selftest and proxy state, then allocates a preferably PMD-aligned physically contiguous region with a page-sized fallback, records base and size, and reports failures without aborting boot.

Finalization is a one-way boot transition guarded by protected and initialized state. It first excludes hypervisor sections and the reserved region from leak checking, enables the protected-mode branch before host stage-two installation, invokes a per-CPU finalize hypercall synchronously and records any failure, and surfaces an error if host privilege drop did not complete.

Protected VM host mapping uses guest frame number and page count to define an inclusive byte interval. Start is the product of frame number and page size, end is the product of frame number plus count and page size minus one, giving contiguous coverage used for range walks and reclamation.

Stage-two table initializer for protected VMs binds the table to its enclosing MMU, initializes an empty cached red-black tree for host-side mappings, ignores allocator operations, and reports success.

Range teardown is idempotent and dossier-local. If a hypervisor VM handle exists and teardown has not started, it starts VM teardown once and marks the VM dying. For protected VMs it reclaims each mapping in the range through a per-page hypercall, checks success, converts frame to struct page, enforces single-page mappings, unpins and accounts the page, removes and frees the tracking node; for non-protected VMs it unshares the range instead. Final page-directory destruction expects no remaining mappings.

Host stage-two helpers reject protected-VM callers where mutation would violate isolation, returning denial or false. Unmap requires write-held MMU lock and unshares the range; write-protect, flush, young-test-clear, relax and mark-young require held MMU lock and iterate intersecting mappings, delegating each to a hypervisor operation or cleaning non-coherent caches when stage-two forced write-back is absent, with relax and mark-young operating on single-page translations.

Unlinked table allocation, freeing and splitting are unsupported in this protected stage-two backend. Each entry warns unconditionally and either returns failure or null, so callers must never rely on them to create or dismantle table levels.

Forced guest-page reclamation issues a hypercall for one physical address and reports success when the hypercall completes or reports transient contention requiring retry, treating both outcomes as reclaim-in-progress rather than failure.
Host PMU registration list is guarded by a global mutex. Initialization takes this mutex while allocating and appending a new host PMU entry, so concurrent registration and traversal do not race.
Named bit constant designates the low bit of perf attribute config word one as the selector for 64-bit counter behavior in the emulated PMU.

Event-type mask starts from EL1 and EL0 exclusion bits plus the VM event-number mask, then conditionally adds EL2 inclusion when the VM advertises that level and adds non-secure EL0, EL1 and EL3 exclusion bits when it advertises EL3, yielding the writable mask for guest event-type registers.

Chaining is permitted only for an even-numbered event counter below the cycle counter that has not recorded a 64-bit overflow, so an overflow in the low half can increment the adjacent odd counter as a combined 64-bit pair.

Counter read resolves a selector to its performance counter object and returns the stored value. Normal write releases any backing host perf event, preserves the upper half on 32-bit guests for event counters unless forced reset is requested, assigns the target system register, and recreates the backing event to reflect the new period. Userspace write releases the backing event, assigns directly, and requests a PMU reload instead of immediate recreation.

Accessible counter mask is the implemented mask reduced for nested guests executing below EL2 by clearing hypervisor-reserved counters; nested EL2 and non-nested guests observe the full implemented mask.

Software counting and host overflow share one increment path gated by global PMU enable and per-counter enable, filtered by masked event type, wrapping to counter width, setting the overflow status bit on wraparound, and recursively incrementing the chained neighbor on chain events. Host overflow additionally stops the backing event, resets its sampling period to the architectural overflow point, requests a pending IRQ when any overflow remains, kicks the vCPU outside NMI context or defers the kick through overflow work inside NMI, then restarts the backing event.

PMCR emulation clears the long-cycle bit when the VM lacks the required PMU version, requests a PMU reload when the global enable toggles, stores the value without the cycle and event reset bits, resets the cycle counter when cycle reset is asked, and resets implemented event counters excluding the cycle and excluding hypervisor-owned counters when below EL2 when event reset is asked, using forced zeroing to clear upper halves.

Event-type programming masks guest data with the VM event-type mask, assigns the per-counter event register, and recreates the backing perf event. Host PMU discovery ignores systems without usable PMUv3 on all CPUs, otherwise allocates a list node under the registration mutex and appends the discovered PMU.
